Command: Cast All Your Care upon Him
Summary: Peter's care command: cast all your care upon him, for he cares for you.
Commandment: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
Application: The command follows humbling under God's hand: care is not carried by willpower but transferred — cast, thrown — onto one who cares. It is the practical side of humility.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'for he careth for you' (1 Peter 5:7).
Function: Care is not carried by willpower but transferred — cast, thrown — onto one who cares. A command of the apostles, not of the Mosaic law, so the threefold division does not sort it. Its goal was relief under God's hand: humble yourselves, and cast all your care upon him, for he careth for you. The evil it addressed was anxiety carried alone, as if no Father were watching. It restrained that evil by the transfer itself: the care goes onto him, because he cares for you.
